To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the fatty acid composition and permeability properties of membranes of Escherichiacoli can be altered by nutrition and that the permeability of membranes is related to the saturated fatty acid content.
the permeability of E. coli cells to small molecules is related to the fatty acid composition (and hence fluidity) of the membrane lipid.

a marked decrease in the percentage of saturated fatty acid of Escherichica coli membrane lipids is associated with a significant decrease in membrane permeability to small molecules and that the permeability of the mutant membranes is less dependent on temperature than that of the wild type membranes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relationship between the fatty acid composition and the permeability properties of the membrane.
a study of the relationship between the structure and function of the membrane lipid of E. coli.
the relationship between fatty acid composition and membrane permeability in E. coli and with the role of fatty acids in membrane function.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the fatty acid composition and the membrane permeability are closely interrelated.

the fatty acid composition in the membrane lipid can influence the permeability of cells to small molecules, and that the extent and nature of the effect depends upon the specific fatty acid composition of membrane lipids.
the fatty acid composition and the permeability of the membrane are closely related, but that the nature of this relation is not clear at present.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the fatty acid composition and the permeability of the cell membrane are closely related.
the fatty acid composition is not the only factor that influences the physical properties of the membrane.
the physical properties of the membrane lipid, and not the chemical nature of the lipid, are the major determinants of the barrier properties of membranes toward small molecules.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the membrane lipid is a very dynamic structure, and the physical properties of the membrane are very responsive to changes in the lipid composition.
the fatty acid composition can be altered to a considerable extent in E. coli mutants without causing any obvious changes in cell growth, cell morphology, cell permeability, or cell viability.
the fatty acid composition and the membrane permeability are not independent of each other.
